guards.what: G1: ThornsPower wired to on_damage_received (killing-blow-guarded, post-block) instead of on_attacked/BeforeDamageReceived-equivalent (unconditional, pre-block, pre-death)
guards.issue: C#'s ThornsPower.BeforeDamageReceived (ThornsPower.cs:17-24) fires unconditionally for every hit, including the hit that kills its owner, and is gated on `props.IsPoweredAttack() || cardSource is Omnislice`. The sim's ThornsPower (sts2_rl/powers.py:328-353) hooks on_damage_received instead, which cmds.py skips entirely on a killing blow (`if not target.is_dead`), and has no IsPoweredAttack/Omnislice gate at all. Pinned with an xfail in test/test_hook_order.py::TestDamagePipelineOrder::test_thorns_reflects_even_on_killing_blow (part a).

guards.what: G3: pipeline-level is_powered_attack(props) gate around the entire modify_damage_additive/multiplicative dispatch, vs C#'s always-call-every-listener-and-self-gate architecture
guards.issue: cmds.py:56-58 skips calling modify_damage_additive/modify_damage_multiplicative for any listener at all when is_powered_attack(props) is false. C#'s ModifyDamageInternal (Hook.cs:2515-2538) always calls every listener's ModifyDamageAdditive/Multiplicative for every damage type, leaving the IsPoweredAttack self-check to each implementation. Strength/Vulnerable/Weak self-gate identically in both codebases (faithful for those three). But the already-ported SurroundedPower (Kaiser Crab back-attack multiplier, sts2_rl/powers.py:2523-2565, mirroring SurroundedPower.cs:46-72) does not self-gate on IsPoweredAttack in either source -- so an Unpowered, dealer-attributed hit against a Surrounded player would still receive the 1.5x multiplier in C# but the sim's pipeline-level gate would skip calling modify_damage_multiplicative entirely, silently dropping it. Currently dormant: Kaiser Crab's own attacks (Rocket.cs) never set the Unpowered flag on their damage.

guards.what: G4: killing-blow post-damage-event skip decision is recomputed after death-prevention resolves in the sim, but is a locked pre-Kill() snapshot in C#
guards.issue: C# decides whether to fire AfterDamageReceived (CreatureCmd.cs:392-399) using WasTargetKilled/IsDead as they stood BEFORE Kill() (and therefore before any ShouldDie/ShouldDieLate listener) runs; a hit that was arithmetically lethal permanently skips AfterDamageReceived even if a listener like LizardTail.ShouldDieLate later prevents the death -- LizardTail instead restores HP via its own separate AfterPreventingDeath hook (LizardTail.cs:49-55), never via AfterDamageReceived. The sim resets HP to 1 first (inside DamageCmd.deal's own apply step) and only afterward checks target.is_dead to decide whether to fire on_damage_received (cmds.py step 7-8) -- so in the sim, a prevented death does NOT skip on_damage_received. Evidenced by the ported LizardTail (sts2_rl/relics/lizard_tail.py, whose own docstring documents relying on this on_damage_received re-fire to perform its heal) combined with any other on_damage_received-gated power active on the same creature at the moment of a prevented killing blow (e.g. the player's own Thorns, per G1, if granted this run) -- that power would incorrectly fire in the sim where C# would not fire the equivalent AfterDamageReceived at all. STRONGER WITNESS (added in review, verified against source): LizardTail + CentennialPuzzle needs no dependency on G1 and uses only already-ported content. C#'s CentennialPuzzle.AfterDamageReceived is itself killing-blow guarded, so on a Lizard-Tail-prevented lethal hit it correctly does not draw; the sim's CentennialPuzzle.on_damage_received (sts2_rl/relics/centennial_puzzle.py:24-35) DOES fire on that hit (hp reset to 1 -> is_dead false -> guard passes) and incorrectly draws 3 cards. Use this pair as the failing test when fixing G4. || RE-AUDIT 2026-07-25 after merging main 7a03d720: G4 STILL STANDS. The death-prevention path was restructured (should_die now takes a `preventer` out-param and a prevented death calls after_preventing_death, cmds.py:96-112) but the substance is unchanged: the sim still sets target.hp = 1 BEFORE step 8 tests `if not target.is_dead`, so a prevented death still fails to skip on_damage_received. Re-verified by reading cmds.py:84-120.

guards.what: G5: DamageCmd.deal has no dealer-is-dead or target-is-dead entry-guard backstop
guards.issue: C#'s CreatureCmd.Damage refuses to process any hit at all from an already-dead dealer (CreatureCmd.cs:242-245, spec step 1) and skips any already-dead target in its per-target loop (CreatureCmd.cs:256-259, spec step 3), both as hard backstops independent of caller discipline. The sim's DamageCmd.deal has neither guard; it relies entirely on call sites to check is_dead between hits of a multi-hit/multi-target attack (e.g. sts2_rl/monsters/base.py:114-117 `_execute_attack`, sts2_rl/cards/whirlwind.py:43-49, both of which currently do this correctly on spot-check). No concrete failure is demonstrated -- this records the structural absence of the pipeline-level backstop, not a proven exploit.

guards.what: G6: dealer-side AfterDamageGiven fires before victim-side AfterDamageReceived in C#; the sim's on_damage_dealt fires after on_damage_received
guards.issue: CreatureCmd.cs:388-395 fires AfterDamageGiven (dealer side, unconditional) before the killing-blow-guarded AfterDamageReceived (victim side). cmds.py's DamageCmd.deal fires on_damage_received (step 8) before on_damage_dealt (step 9) -- the reverse order. Currently dormant: no sim power implements on_damage_dealt yet, so no observable divergence exists with current content, but the pipeline's dispatch order for these two event families is inverted from source and would matter for a dealer-side power/relic that needs to observe pre-victim-reaction state, or vice versa.

guards.what: N1: sim-only should_allow_hitting pre-check has no single C# analogue inside CreatureCmd.Damage
guards.rationale: C# excludes unhittable/reviving creatures upstream, via IsAlive-based target filtering in AttackCommand.GetPossibleTargets (AttackCommand.cs:544-546) plus real-death semantics for reviving Decimillipede-style segments, rather than a dedicated hook inside CreatureCmd.Damage itself. The sim's should_allow_hitting hook (used only by MockRevivePower/ReattachPower-family reviving-segment logic, sts2_rl/powers.py:1572-1575, 2354-2357, 3372-3375) re-architects this as an explicit pipeline predicate. Net effect is equivalent for the currently-ported content (Decimillipede); documented so a future audit doesn't mistake it for an unmapped C# hook.

guards.what: N2: DamageCmd.deal takes a single Creature per call; CreatureCmd.Damage batches IEnumerable<Creature> and defers all targets' step-17/18 events until every target in the call has resolved blocking/HP-loss
guards.rationale: The sim's callers (card code, Monster._execute_attack) loop over multiple simultaneous targets themselves, each a fully independent DamageCmd.deal call including its own Kill() processing, rather than the pipeline batching them. For a C# attack that hits several creatures at once, every target's AfterDamageGiven/AfterDamageReceived-or-skip resolves before ANY of them is actually Kill()'d; in the sim, the first target's entire pipeline (including death processing) completes before the second target's begins. No concretely broken current interaction was found (the one candidate, Decimillipede's ReattachPower 'are all other segments dead' check, is evaluated on a segment's own later turn, well after any same-turn AOE has already fully resolved in both architectures), but this is a real structural difference. Cross-reference: primarily the concern of the creature_card_cmds seam (Task 7), which owns how cards orchestrate multi-target attacks; recorded here because it originates in DamageCmd.deal's own signature.

guards.what: N3 (LIVE): additive/multiplicative dispatch is a parallel sum/product in the sim vs a sequential running-value chain in C# -- RAISED from deliberate-divergence to gap in the Task 9 fix pass
guards.issue: Hook.cs:2515-2538 (ModifyDamageInternal) passes the RUNNING total to each successive ModifyDamageAdditive/Multiplicative call and folds the result in immediately, in decimal. sts2_rl/hooks.py:52-78 instead passes every listener the SAME pre-step base and sums/multiplies the returns independently, and cmds.py:57-58 applies the aggregate once: `amount = amount + hooks.modify_damage_additive(...)` then `amount = int(amount * hooks.modify_damage_multiplicative(...))`. This includes card-enchantment bonuses, which the sim registers as ordinary hooks (combat.py:133) rather than as C#'s explicit pre-step (Hook.cs:1490-1499). PREVIOUSLY RECORDED AS deliberate-divergence on the argument that every ported implementation returns a value independent of the running amount. That argument is sound as far as it goes and was re-verified in the fix pass (`py audit/tools/dormancy_probes.py cs-running-value` / `sim-running-value`: 0 of 46 C# overrides and 0 of 9 C# Enchant* overrides and 0 of 31 sim implementations read the value handed to them) -- but it settles only the ARGUMENT, not the AGGREGATION SHAPE, and the shape diverges on its own. The additive family is safe (base + sum(a_i) == the sequential fold, exhaustively checked, 0 mismatches). The multiplicative family is NOT: the sim multiplies the factors together in FLOAT and applies the product once, where C# folds each factor into the running decimal. LIVE and EXECUTED: Shrink (x0.7 on the dealer, applied by the ported Act-1 Shrinker Beetle monsters/overgrowth/shrinker_beetle.py:39-40 and by the Shrink Potion, powers.py:1366-1387) plus Vulnerable (x1.5 on the target, powers.py:403-417) on a 20-damage powered attack deals 20 in the sim and 21 in the game -- sim 1.5*0.7 = 1.0499999999999998, 20*that = 20.999999999999996, int -> 20; game 20m*1.5m = 30m, 30m*0.7m = 21m. Base 40 diverges the same way (41 vs 42). A control that keeps the sim's float arithmetic but threads it sequentially returns 21, so this is the aggregation shape and not float-vs-decimal representation. SAME MECHANISM, SAME VERDICT AT EVERY SITE (rule 3): audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json step 31 is the machinery statement and carries the identical gap; the BLOCK site (Hook.cs:1320-1337 vs hooks.py:98-122 + cmds.py:145-147) is creature_card_cmds' step 13, AMENDED (fix pass 2): it carries the identical gap, but is DORMANT there -- all five ported block multipliers return only {0.0, 0.75, 2.0}, every one dyadic, and an exhaustive sweep of 15 ordered subsets x bases 0-999 found 0 mismatches between the sim's product and C#'s sequential decimal. A non-dyadic block multiplier would make it live; the only one in the source is MultiplayerScalingModel.cs:52-68, waived under N1. Pinned by test/test_hook_order.py::TestHookDispatchOrder::test_multiplicative_damage_modifiers_chain_sequentially (strict xfail).

guards.what: N4: C#'s ShouldDie (early) / ShouldDieLate (late) two-phase death-prevention priority collapsed to a single flat pass in the sim
guards.rationale: Hook.cs:2229-2249 runs all ShouldDie listeners first, then all ShouldDieLate listeners, so an early preventer always gets first refusal over a Late one (LizardTail is explicitly ShouldDieLate so other prevention effects trigger first, per its own doc comment). sts2_rl/hooks.py's should_die (line 565) has one flat pass. Not reachable in the current Ironclad-only sim: the only non-mock, non-potion ShouldDie/ShouldDieLate listener in the whole C# codebase is LizardTail itself (ShouldDieLate); FairyInABottle (ShouldDie) is a potion (out of scope). With a single listener, the two-phase ordering has no listener to order against.

guards.what: N5: on_block_broken fires during block absorption (before HP loss is applied) in the sim; AfterBlockBroken fires after HP loss is applied in C#
guards.rationale: cmds.py step 4 fires on_block_broken immediately when block hits exactly 0 during absorption; CreatureCmd.cs:376-379 fires AfterBlockBroken later, in the second per-result loop, after LoseHpInternal has already mutated CurrentHp (step 13). Both fire unconditionally regardless of whether the same hit also kills the target. Currently ported listeners (StunPower-on-block-break in sts2_rl/powers.py:2293-2300, Hand Drill in sts2_rl/relics/hand_drill.py:21-29) read neither HP nor death state, so no observable difference exists today.
